sections.title: Save our park!

q.prompt: Which word means “make someone agree with you or do something”?

options.fb: “campaign” means planned actions to change something.

q.prompt: What does the council want to build?

captions: Hello, and welcome to Atomic English, Stage 5. In this lesson: Save our park!
Recognise persuasive language and use the first conditional.
Here are some new words. Persuade. Make someone agree with you or do something. Campaign.
Planned actions to change something. Protect. Keep something safe. Listen and say them.
persuade
campaign
protect.
And some more words. Wildlife. Animals and plants that live in nature. Council.
The people who make decisions for a town. Petition.
A letter signed by many people asking for a change. Listen and say them. wildlife
council
petition.
Time for a question. The video will stop.
Which word means: make someone agree with you or do something?
Now some grammar: First conditional. Use If, plus the present simple, then will,
plus a verb, for real possibilities in the future.
For example: If we lose the park, the birds will lose their homes.
For example: If you sign the petition, you will help.
Now listen, and read along. Save Greenfield Park! Save Greenfield Park!
The town council wants to build a car park where Greenfield Park is now.
We think this is a terrible idea.
Greenfield Park is home to foxes, hedgehogs and more than twenty kinds of birds.
If the park disappears, this wildlife will lose its home.
Every day, hundreds of children play here. Where will they go if the park closes?
Do you want more cars and more pollution in our town? Of course not!
Please sign our petition before 30th June. Together, we can protect our park!
Another question. The video will stop. What does the council want to build?
Well done! Today you learned new words, like persuade, campaign, protect.
You practised the first conditional. And you read Save Greenfield Park!
Now try the practice questions. See you next time!

captions: Hello, and welcome to Atomic English, Stage 5. In this lesson: Fact or opinion?
Tell facts from opinions and use persuasive words in an advert.
Here are some new words. Advert. A picture or film that tries to sell something. Product.
Something that is made to be sold. Customer. A person who buys something.
Listen and say them. advert
product
customer.
And some more words. Bargain. Something sold for less than its usual price. Amazing.
Very surprising and wonderful. Guarantee. A promise that something will work.
Listen and say them. bargain
amazing
guarantee.
Time for a question. The video will stop.
Which word means: a picture or film that tries to sell something?
Now some grammar: Fact or opinion. A fact can be checked and proved.
An opinion is what someone thinks or feels.
Opinions often use words like best, amazing, I think.
For example: Fact: The bike weighs 9 kilograms.
For example: Opinion: It is the best bike ever.
Now listen, and read along. SuperGlow school bag.
Introducing the SuperGlow school bag – the coolest bag you will ever own!
It has three big pockets and a special pocket for your water bottle.
The straps glow in the dark, so drivers can see you on dark winter mornings.
It is made from recycled plastic bottles – twelve bottles in every bag!
Only 25 đô la this month – what a bargain!
If you don't love it, we will give you your money back. That's our guarantee!
Another question. The video will stop. How many big pockets does the bag have?
Well done! Today you learned new words, like advert, product, customer.
You practised fact or opinion. And you read SuperGlow school bag.
Now try the practice questions. See you next time!
